title: Sample-driven precision-path negotiator and accuracy-gated kernel routing
creator: Alejandro Ruiz
description:
Goal: Implement a runtime component (Precision Path Negotiator) that chooses between FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernel paths per-request and per-layer using a lightweight sample-driven calibration and accuracy gating mechanism. This ticket covers the negotiation protocol, calibration sample orchestration, accuracy validation integration, and the fallback policies used when an accuracy gate fails or latency/cost constraints bind.

Context: We already have offline quant profiles (per-model, per-layer INT8 and FP8 candidates) produced by the quantization pipeline. However, runtime selection today is static (model-level) and cannot react to input distribution shifts, batch size, or SLO constraints. The negotiator must enable dynamic per-request routing to heterogeneous kernels while ensuring end-to-end quality and predictable latency/cost.

High-level approach:
- During model load, attach metadata: available quant profiles, expected calibration summary stats (histograms, outlier counts), and a compact validation fingerprint.
- For live traffic, the negotiator samples a configurable fraction of requests for shadow execution across candidate precision paths (micro-canary). Shadow results are validated against quality evaluators (log-likelihood delta, token-level edit distance, and domain-specific eval hooks).
- Accuracy gates: candidate path passes if validation metrics stay within configured deltas for a moving window. If a path fails, it is temporarily blacklisted and traffic routed to the next-best path (cost-aware).
- Cost/latency model: the negotiator consults a local cost estimator (token-per-second and GPU-cycle proxy) to weigh latency SLO vs. unit cost; it supports policy profiles (aggressive-cost, latency-first, balanced).
- Fallbacks: graceful rollback to FP16 or a conservatively quantized INT8 fallback with prefix caching reuse. Support exponential backoff for re-probing failed paths.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: kernel-level micro-optimizations, offline quant profile creation (handled by quant pipeline), and UI for console (will be separate PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator can be enabled via model config and selects a kernel path at request time based on policy and recent validation state.
Sampling harness can shadow up to 5% of traffic and execute candidate kernels without affecting primary output latency.
Accuracy gate evaluates shadow outputs with at least three metrics (perplexity delta, token edit distance, and optional domain callback) and produces pass/fail decisions with configurable thresholds.
Failed paths are blacklisted for a configurable cooldown and automatically re-probed with exponentially decaying frequency.
End-to-end e2e tests that simulate distribution shift trigger path changes and demonstrate that accuracy remains within configured deltas while cost drops under the balanced policy.
Telemetry: per-path success rate, sample rate, average latency, cost-savings estimate, and blacklist events appear in the runtime metrics endpoint.
No regression to existing FP16-only workloads when negotiator is disabled (backward compatible).
tasks: Design negotiator config schema (model metadata and runtime flags) and document in design doc (link below)
Implement lightweight sample executor that runs shadow kernels in a lower-priority work-queue
Integrate accuracy validator module with hooks for perplexity, token-edit-distance, and custom evaluator callbacks
Build local cost/latency estimator and policy comparator (aggressive-cost/latency-first/balanced)
Implement blacklist + re-probe state machine with persistence to node-level snapshot
Add runtime metrics and tracing spans for negotiation decisions (Prometheus + Jaeger tags)
End-to-end integration tests + synthetic distribution-shift harness
Benchmark mixed-precision throughput/latency overhead for sample execution at 1%, 3%, and 5% sampling rates
